headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman outlines [[3-R strategy to rebuild Bangladesh]] in UNGA address
headline: PM Tarique Rahman outlines 3-R strategy to rebuild Bangladesh in UNGA address
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addressed the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, detailing plans for recovery, restoration, and reconstruction after years of exploitation.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced his government's 3-R strategy—recovery, restoration, and reconstruction—to rebuild Bangladesh. This initiative aims to repair the nation following more than a decade and a half of what he described as fascist rule and exploitation.

Addressing the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, the Prime Minister stated that Bangladesh is now re-embarking on the path of democracy. He highlighted the country's liberation from enforced disappearances, killings, abductions, corruption, looting, and money laundering.

An immense horizon of possibilities has opened for Bangladesh, with the government implementing extensive programs to transform the working-age population into skilled human resources. This leverages the demographic dividend, aiming to develop Bangladesh as a 'manufacturing hub' and create widespread employment opportunities.

The government has allocated US$50 million in the current fiscal year to support young entrepreneurs, researchers, and innovators in their start-up initiatives. Prime Minister Rahman sought support from Bangladesh's development partners for these endeavors.

Emphasizing women's empowerment, Tarique Rahman noted that women constitute over half of Bangladesh's population and are central to all government plans for socio-economic transformation. Priorities include expanded opportunities for women's education, employment, and entrepreneurship, particularly in small and medium-sized industries.

Free education opportunities for women up to the undergraduate level have also been made available. The government aims to ensure not only electoral democracy but also the democratisation of the economy, ensuring that the benefits of growth reach every family and citizen.

To achieve this, social protection initiatives like the Family Card, Farmers' Card, Sports Card, and e-Health Card have been introduced for economically disadvantaged people. The Family Card, issued to the female head of each household, symbolizes women's economic empowerment, with plans for a future Universal Card.

The government is implementing its 31-point program, presented before the February 12 national election, with 73 percent directly aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals' "Leave No One Behind" theme. Another 27 percent are indirectly aligned, aiming to reduce urban-rural disparities and advance inclusive sustainable development.

Special importance has been given to education, health, and sports, with the highest-ever budget allocation for education. Plans include gradually increasing education spending to 5 percent of GDP within five years, alongside a new curriculum emphasizing technical and practical education.

Primary students from the first grade receive school bags, uniforms, and free midday meals to boost enrollment and quality. Sports has also been integrated into the education curriculum for the first time, aiming to establish it as a profession, as evidenced by a nationwide football tournament involving over two million students.

headline_marked: [[Housewife gang-raped in Manikganj]], chili powder thrown on her body
headline: Housewife gang-raped in Manikganj, chili powder thrown on her body
summary: A woman in Singair was allegedly abducted from her home, gang-raped, and then had her hands and feet tied with chili powder sprinkled on her body. She has since filed a police report.
details: An alarming incident has been reported in Singair, Manikganj, where a housewife was allegedly gang-raped by five masked individuals. Following the assault, the perpetrators reportedly tied her hands and feet and sprinkled chili powder on her body.
The victim filed a case with the police on Thursday. According to her statement, the incident occurred on September 21, late at night, when she stepped out of her house to answer nature's call.

Five masked individuals, who had been lying in wait, allegedly grabbed her, covered her mouth, and forcibly took her about 100 yards away to an agricultural field. There, they threatened her with sharp weapons and gang-raped her.
After the assault, the assailants used clothes and an orna to tie her hands and feet. They then sprinkled dry chili powder on her face, eyes, and body before fleeing the scene.

Her relatives, alerted by her screams, rescued her from the location and immediately took her to the Upazila Health Complex for treatment. The victim described the suspects as being between 15 and 25 years old, speaking in a local dialect.

Assistant Superintendent of Police Fahim Asjad of Singair Circle confirmed that the woman received medical attention. He stated that while a case has been filed, no arrests have been made yet, and police are actively working to identify and apprehend the suspects.
